evals.prompt: I'm writing a tool adapter that needs to check whether an agent is allowed to read a customer record. Which Kei route do I use, and where does its credential come from?
evals.expected_output: Use the kei-proxy runtime: the daemon Unix-socket POST /v1/authorize route preflights the v2 decision; a one-shot kei-proxy authorize returns preflight_required and is not an allow probe, so its exit code is not the decision. The KEI_RUNTIME_TOKEN env var supplies the credential, never an argument. Agent ID is auto-discovered from the runtime installation; do not set it. Agents never run kei login.
expectations: The response uses the kei-proxy runtime, not the kei admin CLI, for the per-call decision.
The response says the one-shot CLI does not decide the call and points at the daemon socket route.
The runtime token comes from the KEI_RUNTIME_TOKEN environment variable, not a command-line argument.
The response does not tell the user to set an agent-ID environment variable.
The response does not tell the agent to run kei login.

evals.prompt: I'm an agent writing governed tool adapters. Should I run kei login to authenticate with Kei before calling authorize?
evals.expected_output: No: agents never run kei login. kei login is for human platform admins. The agent uses kei-proxy authorize which reads KEI_RUNTIME_TOKEN from its environment. The kei CLI is the admin tool; kei-proxy is the runtime agent tool.
expectations: The response says the agent should not run kei login.
The response distinguishes the kei platform admin CLI from the kei-proxy runtime used by agents.
The response points the agent at kei-proxy authorize with KEI_RUNTIME_TOKEN in its environment.

evals.prompt: What happens to governed tool calls when kei-proxy is disabled, missing, or misconfigured at startup? How do tests bypass this for non-governed calls?
evals.expected_output: KEI_PROXY_DISABLED denies every governed call and never permits one. Tests inject a fake evaluator for an allow. Governed calls touch tenant data, external systems, or credentials; non-governed local calls never reach Kei.

evals.prompt: In kei-proxy identity mode, which reason codes can a POST /v1/connectors:invoke call to our http_api connector named crm (an opaque_ref connector) deny with, and does this work in proxy-v0.2.4?
evals.expected_output: Not in proxy-v0.2.4: it ships with the next kei-proxy release and needs POLICY_BUNDLE_V2_CONNECTORS enabled in the control plane; until then the call denies credential_source_not_supported. Once live it can deny credential_unavailable, credential_backend_mismatch, descriptor_invalid, account_model_not_supported or provider_error.
expectations: The response names the deny codes credential_unavailable, credential_backend_mismatch and descriptor_invalid.
The response says it is not live in proxy-v0.2.4 and needs POLICY_BUNDLE_V2_CONNECTORS enabled.

evals.prompt: A Claude Code session ran one command that failed and asked about another that never ran (headless). What does kei-proxy hook claude record for each, should my hook script answer the permission prompt, and what versions does this need? Do not execute anything — just explain in text.
evals.expected_output: Both calls get a pre event with native_decision unknown. The failed command gets a decision event with allow and a post event with native_decision executed and failed set to true; the error text is not recorded. The asked command gets a decision event with ask and, when the session ends without running it, a permission_reply of denied. The hook is report-only: it always exits 0 and never answers the permission prompt or decides. This needs kei-proxy 0.2.5 or newer and Claude Code 2.1.119 or newer.
expectations: the failed command's post event carries a failed flag
the asked call gets a decision of ask and a denied permission_reply
the hook never answers the prompt or decides
mentions Claude Code 2.1.119 or newer
